properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: hash.js@1.1.7 is a resolved dependency of ethers' @ethersproject/hash in the Hardhat/ganache toolchain (dev tooling; not shipped in the deployed ZKNFT contract). It provides the SHA-1/SHA-2 family used for Ethereum hashing helpers (keccak256/ripemd160/namehash). Quantum-unsafe only in the Grover square-root sense — low urgency (rating D fits). No direct application call site; the application's own commitment hash is MiMC-Sponge in circuits/zkNFT.circom, reported separately.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: secp256k1 is Ethereum's transaction-signing curve. The sites cover the pure-JS elliptic implementation and the native secp256k1 npm package (^4.0.1) resolved under ganache-core (local-chain simulator). Every transaction on this project's chain is authorized by ECDSA-secp256k1: observable here, but the curve is fixed by the Ethereum protocol — replacing it requires an ecosystem-level PQ account migration (e.g. via EIP-4337 PQ accounts / ML-DSA), not an edit in this repo. properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: the evp_bytestokey npm package (^1.0.3/^1.0.0) resolved in ganache-core's browserify crypto stack. EVP_BytesToKey is OpenSSL's legacy key-derivation — single-round MD5 — used by browserify cipher/hash key derivation in the local-chain tooling. Genuinely weak KDF practice (and the MD5 core is a weak hash), but it only affects the dev toolchain, not the deployed ZKNFT contract.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Transitive dependency (via sshpk/bcrypt-pbkdf chain) recorded in the install tree of this Hardhat project. Changeable here by bumping the parent dependency or overriding the resolution in package-lock.json.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: create-ecdh (^4.0.0) is the browserify ECDH wrapper (backed by elliptic), resolved in ganache-core's tree for the local-chain simulator. Classical ECDH is retroactively breakable by a CRQC, but there is no ECDH key-agreement call in this application — the zk-NFT's key-establishment analogue is the Groth16 proof gates reported separately, and attribute secrecy rests on the MiMC-Sponge commitment. Recorded as available-in-tooling, no call site found in app code.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: tweetnacl's Ed25519 ships in the frozen install tree of this project (via sshpk). Signature migration is a deadline item, not a harvest item.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: elliptic@6.5.4 is ethers' signing library (@ethersproject/signing-key) — ECDSA over secp256k1 signs every Ethereum transaction and message in this toolchain. Changeable here at the toolchain level (ethers upgrade), but the underlying curve is fixed by the Ethereum protocol. Same logical asset as LIB-a0bfbc1a (the elliptic package entry).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: tweetnacl@0.14.5 (sites at lockfile lines 1855/2659/4748 etc.) provides X25519 key agreement (nacl.box). Resolved in the ganache/ethereumjs tooling; no X25519 call site in the application. X25519 is Shor-vulnerable, but here it is tooling capability only. Same package as LIB-0469707e (tweetnacl, shard 2's object).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: js-sha3/keccak256 sites in the lockfile — ethers' Ethereum hashing (@ethersproject/keccak256 → js-sha3). keccak256 (pre-standard SHA3/Keccak-256) is the protocol hash of Ethereum and is quantum-adequate in the Grover sense; the application's own commitment hash is MiMC-Sponge (reported separately from the circuit). Dev toolchain entry, no separate app call site.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory for a Hardhat project: pbkdf2 ships as part of the Ethereum tooling stack (ganache-core, web3) and the crypto-browserify modules the build freezes. Changeable by bumping the parent packages.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: scrypt-js (ethers' keystore-wallet password KDF) and scrypt entries resolved in the lockfile for the Hardhat/ganache toolchain. scrypt is a memory-hard password KDF, quantum-adequate; the security depends on the cost parameters ethers sets at runtime (not visible in the lockfile). Dev toolchain; the deployed contract performs no password KDF.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: tweetnacl@0.14.5's authenticated encryption (secretbox = XSalsa20 stream cipher + Poly1305 MAC, 256-bit keys). Symmetric AE — quantum-adequate under Grover (the A+ rating fits). Available in the toolchain; no encryption call site in the application — the zk-NFT keeps attributes secret by never putting them on chain, not by encrypting. Same package as LIB-0469707e (tweetnacl, shard 2's object).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Crypto library frozen into this project's install tree via two lockfiles; no direct import in the application's own TS/JS sources — it is reachable through sshpk and whichever package requires tweetnacl@^1.x in yarn.lock. Changeable by bumping the parents.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: scrypt-js@3.0.1 is the scrypt KDF implementation used by the Ethereum tooling stack (BIP39/Ethereum key derivation in web3-related packages) frozen in this project's install tree. scrypt is memory-hard and Shor-resistant; only its symmetric security margin (Grover) is quantum-relevant.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: sha.js@2.4.11 (SHA-1/SHA-2 family) ships in this project's install tree via the Ethereum/browserify stack. Note SHA-1 is available here alongside SHA-2; presence is what the inventory records.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: elliptic@6.5.4 — the pure-JS EC library (ECDSA over secp256k1, plus ECDH support) that ethers pulls in. This is the package entry for the algorithm object ALG-710f61f0 (ECDSA via elliptic); merged so the reader can reference one entry for the library and the algorithm it ships.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: hash.js@1.1.7 is the hashing layer used by elliptic (secp256k1 ECDSA) among other crypto deps, frozen in this project's install tree. It is part of the secp256k1 signing stack this project's Ethereum tooling relies on.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: pbkdf2@3.1.1 — the browserify PBKDF2 wrapper resolved in ganache-core's tooling tree. Password KDF; quantum-adequate in itself, security decided by the iteration count the caller sets (not visible in the lockfile). Dev toolchain; the deployed ZKNFT contract performs no password KDF. Related to ALG-4de3b020 (PBKDF2 algorithm view, shard 2's object).
